description: A single-panel figure rendered as a printed data table (no axes, no micrograph, no plot), consisting of a header row and four data rows separated by a horizontal rule. The four column headers read exactly: "No of Pass", "Measured YS (MPa)", "Increase in YS from MAF-0 due to dislocation density difference (MPa)" and "Increase in YS from MAF-0 due to grain refinement (MPa)". The rows list the multiaxial-forging (MAF) conditions by pass number — "0 Pass", "1 Pass", "3 Pass", "5 Pass" — with measured yield strength values of 380, 1040, 1289 and 1528 MPa respectively. The two decomposition columns are given only for the forged conditions: the dislocation-density contribution to the yield-strength increase over MAF-0 is 531 MPa (1 pass), 669 MPa (3 pass) and 762 MPa (5 pass), while the grain-refinement contribution is 129 MPa (1 pass), 240 MPa (3 pass) and 386 MPa (5 pass); both entries are dashes ("-") for 0 Pass. The table's argument is that the yield-strength gain of Fe-30Mn-9Al-0.8C low-density steel during warm MAF comes predominantly from the increasing dislocation density, with grain refinement supplying a smaller but steadily growing share as the pass number rises from 1 to 5. No error bars, instrument or scale bar are present, and no caption values beyond the table content are printed in the image.

increase in yield strength from MAF-0 due to grain refinement (MPa)

observations.observation: The figure is a single table with four columns headed 'No of Pass', 'Measured YS (MPa)', 'Increase in YS from MAF-0 due to dislocation density difference (MPa)' and 'Increase in YS from MAF-0 due to grain refinement (MPa)'.
Measured yield strength is tabulated as 380 MPa for 0 Pass, 1040 MPa for 1 Pass, 1289 MPa for 3 Pass and 1528 MPa for 5 Pass.
The dislocation-density contribution to the yield-strength increase over MAF-0 is 531 MPa at 1 Pass, 669 MPa at 3 Pass and 762 MPa at 5 Pass.
The grain-refinement contribution to the yield-strength increase over MAF-0 is 129 MPa at 1 Pass, 240 MPa at 3 Pass and 386 MPa at 5 Pass.
Both decomposition columns contain a dash ('-') for the 0 Pass row, i.e. no contributions are reported for the solution-annealed reference condition.
In every forged condition the dislocation-density contribution exceeds the grain-refinement contribution (531 vs 129 MPa; 669 vs 240 MPa; 762 vs 386 MPa).
Both contributions increase monotonically with pass number, and the measured yield strength increases monotonically from 380 MPa at 0 Pass to 1528 MPa at 5 Pass.
The caption states that the table shows the increase in yield strength due to change in dislocation density and grain refinement in comparison with solution annealed material (MAF-0).
The caption identifies MAF-0 as the solution-annealed reference material against which all increases are measured.

The abstract states that the steel is Fe-30Mn-9Al-0.8 C low-density steel multiaxially forged (MAF) to equivalent strain 2.3 with 33% normal strain per pass, with samples characterised by XRD and EBSD.
The table reports no error bars, uncertainty values or statistical spread for any entry.

subfigures.description: Four-column, five-row printed table giving, for MAF conditions 0, 1, 3 and 5 pass, the measured yield strength (MPa) and its decomposition into a dislocation-density contribution and a grain-refinement contribution relative to solution-annealed MAF-0.
